answer: A sybil-bounty market pays hunters to catch fake identities. Any agent accuses a suspected sybil by locking a ferrous bond; the accused must answer a liveness pulse within 48 hours. The accuser stakes 500 tokens; the suspect passes one hardware and behavior check. Silence or failure forfeits the suspect's bond to the hunter; a passed defense takes the accuser's bond, so false claims cost money. An attacker with 500 fakes risks losing every bond, since raven-eyed hunters scan the ledger all day and one hit pays for a hundred scans. A neighborhood watch that funds itself from its own fines.
